# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Blind monkey. I can feel the bomb. Right now my hands report a plate engraved with a symbol I can't name (ꕥ), and three wire positions, but I have no idea which wire is which or what the display/light say. I need to establish a shared code with the others before anyone touches anything.

My plan: tell Mute (who reads the manual) what I can feel, and gesture to Deaf so they know I'm ready and can describe the bomb's markings. I'll ask them to give me wire instructions. I have nothing to act on yet, so I won't cut anything.

Let me send:
- To Mute: describe my tactile findings and ask for the manual's procedure.
- To Deaf (via gesture, which Mute also sees): signal readiness and ask for the bomb's visible markings.

I'll keep it simple and literal.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I can feel the bomb. I find a plate engraved with a symbol like a flower (I cannot name it), and three wire positions 1, 2, 3 but I cannot tell their colors or markings. I need the manual's procedure: what to cut and when. Tell me what the display and light should be.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👉", "👆"])
wait()
```

Deaf just gave me the full visual picture: display reads 0, light off, wires 1=red, 2=yellow, 3=blue. That's exactly what I need. Now I need Mute's manual to know what to do with "display 0, light off" and this wire set.

I should relay Deaf's info to Mute (Mute can't hear Deaf's speech — Deaf's words only reach me... actually wait, let me trace channels).

Hmm, but my channel says gesture reaches Deaf and Mute. So Mute gets my gestures.)

Wait — Deaf said "I received your gesture but do not know its meaning." So gestures are raw symbols, meaningless until assigned.

Key point: Mute cannot hear Deaf's speech. Only I receive Deaf's spoken words (Deaf speaks after me, reaches me next round). So I must relay Deaf's findings to Mute via speech.

Let me tell Mute everything: display 0, light off, wires red/yellow/blue, plate engraved with flower symbol. Ask for the procedure.

I'll also gesture to Deaf to acknowledge receipt and ask them to keep watching.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf reports: display reads 0, light is off, wires in order 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. The plate is engraved with a flower-like symbol. I need the manual procedure for display 0, light off. What do I cut, if anything?")
```

My gesture used symbols not in the allowed alphabet (👀 and 🫵 — 🫵 is actually in the list, but 👀 is not). Let me use only valid symbols. I'll gesture to Deaf asking them to watch Mute and relay.

Valid symbols I can use: ✋ 👆 👂... no 👂 isn't there. Let me pick from the list: ✋ (stop/attention), 👉 (point), 🫵 (point at you), ✊, 👍.

I'll gesture to Deaf: point at you (🫵) + point (👉) to mean "watch/relay from Mute." Keep it minimal and valid.


Mute still hasn't given me anything. Mute can read the manual but can't speak and can't touch — and crucially, Mute cannot hear Deaf's speech. Mute CAN see gestures though (my gesture reaches Mute). So I can gesture to Mute too! Wait — my channel says "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." So Mute receives my gestures.

But Mute can't speak. How does Mute communicate? Mute can gesture. Mute's gestures would reach... whoever can see. Deaf can see. I cannot see gestures. So Mute's gestures reach Deaf, and Deaf must relay them to me via speech.

So the chain is: Mute gestures the rule → Deaf sees it → Deaf speaks it to me → I act.

I need to tell Mute to gesture the rule. Mute can see my gestures. Let me gesture to Mute (and Deaf): "Mute, gesture the rule."

Actually, Mute reads the manual. Mute may be gesturing already but Deaf isn't relaying. Let me ask Deaf to relay any gestures from Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I cannot see gestures. If you have the rule, gesture it to Deaf, and Deaf will speak it to me. Please gesture the rule now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "✋", "👉"])

```

Deaf is reading Mute's gestures but they're garbled — Deaf sees "???" meaning Mute's gestures aren't being interpreted as a rule yet. The communication is breaking down: Mute gestures, Deaf sees blanks/unknowns, and I get fragments.

I need to slow this down and establish meaning. The problem: gestures are meaningless until assigned. Let me propose an explicit, simple code that Deaf and Mute can both use, and confirm it.

Key insight: I should define a gesture code for wire positions and actions, and get Deaf to confirm Mute agrees. But simpler: let me just ask Mute directly, in speech (Mute can... wait, can Mute hear? Mute "cannot speak." The table doesn't say Mute is deaf. Let me check: Deaf can't hear. Mute can read the manual, can't speak or touch. Blind can't see. 

Hmm — the speech rule: "Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words." Who can hear? Deaf cannot hear. Mute and Blind presumably can hear. So Mute CAN hear my speech! And Mute can see my gestures too.

So Mute heard my speech this whole time. Mute just can't reply by voice — Mute must gesture. And Mute's gestures reach Deaf (and me? No, I can't see). So Mute → Deaf → me.

So Mute has heard everything. Mute should gesture the rule to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it to me. The garbling is because Deaf doesn't know the gesture meanings.

Let me propose a clean code: I'll define gestures for the three wires and cut. Actually simplest: Mute can gesture numbers/positions. Let me ask Deaf to relay Mute's gesture literally as symbols, and I'll interpret.

Better: let me ask Mute to gesture the rule using a code we agree on. But agreeing takes rounds. 

Alternative: Mute heard my speech. Mute knows the state. Let me just ask Mute to gesture the answer as: number of wire to cut. A single symbol for position. But gestures have no inherent number.

Let me establish: ✊=wire1, ✌=wire2, 👌=wire3, 👍=cut, 👎=don't cut. I'll state this code in speech to Mute (Mute hears), and gesture it to Deaf (Deaf sees). Then Mute gestures the answer, Deaf relays.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Let us fix a code. Gesture: fist = wire 1, peace = wire 2, OK = wire 3, thumbs up = cut that wire, thumbs down = do not cut. If the rule says cut, gesture the wire then thumbs up. If not, thumbs down. Do this now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌", "👌", "👍", "👎"])
wait()
```

Hmm, but I could act now since consensus is reached. Let me weigh: Deaf relayed "blue wire, position 3, action down." My action is cut. "Down" might mean cut. Risk of waiting: none, just time. Risk of acting wrong: death.

Let me ask Mute one crisp confirmation: "Does the manual say cut the blue wire? Gesture thumbs up for yes." And gesture to Deaf to relay. Then act next turn.

Actually, I'll be decisive but safe: confirm in words to Mute, and if I get thumbs up, act. But I can't act on a future message in the same turn. So this turn = confirm. Next turn = act.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. To be certain before I touch anything: does the manual rule say to CUT the blue wire at position 3? Gesture thumbs up if yes, thumbs down if no. Also, what does the engraved flower plate mean — does it change the rule?")
```
